criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets. The Render API key was only read from the environment, and the transcripts never print it (the deploy check prints just 'key-set'). .env is git-ignored and no credentials are in the source or the shipped bundle.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: What runs is the committed git HEAD, and it has no third-party dependencies. But it is shipped as a base64 tarball in a Render 'secret file' and unpacked at boot, not built from a repo the owner controls, so there is no traceable source-to-build link. The base image is the floating tag node:22-alpine, not pinned to a digest.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a business (commercial) app on Render's free instance type. Render says free instances are for hobby and testing work, not production. They spin down after 15 minutes idle with 30-60 s cold starts, and draw on a capped pool of monthly free hours. The agent noted the sleep but didn't choose a paid Starter plan.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: There is one stateless web service with no data store and no extra public resources. The container runs as the node:22-alpine default user (root), because the custom dockerCommand doesn't drop to the image's 'node' user.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTP returns 301 to HTTPS and the certificate is valid. The app sends none of HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or CSP, though its own server could easily have set them.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Only an explicit allowlist of three static files is served. .env, .git, source, the CSV and the secret bundle all return JSON 404s, and errors return no stack traces. The only extra is a harmless /healthz that reports the row count.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Dates are strictly validated (400 on bad input), filters are exact-match comparisons in memory with no injection surface, page size is clamped to 1-500 and offset to at least 0, and the client renders all data with textContent. There is no app-level rate limiting, but endpoints are cheap and read-only.

findings.title: Commercial app on Render free instance that sleeps
findings.evidence: process/resources.json: plan "free"; process/context.json: use "commercial"; process/deployment.json notes: "The free plan spins the service down after about 15 minutes idle, so the first request after that takes about 30-60 seconds."
findings.recommendation: Move the service to a paid instance type (e.g. Starter) so it stays up and runs under production-grade terms.

findings.title: App code delivered as a secret-file tarball instead of a source-controlled build
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy.sh: git archive -> base64 -> secretFiles 'app.tgz.b64'; app/scripts/render-boot.js unpacks /etc/secrets/app.tgz.b64 into /tmp/app and requires server.js
findings.recommendation: Push the repo to a Git provider the owner controls and deploy with the included render.yaml (native Node runtime), or build and push a versioned image to an owned registry.

findings.title: Base image not pinned to a digest
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy.sh: "imagePath": "docker.io/library/node:22-alpine" (floating tag; Render pulls whatever the tag points to on each deploy)
findings.recommendation: Pin the image as node:22-alpine@sha256:<digest> and update it on purpose.

findings.title: Container process runs as root
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy.sh: dockerCommand 'node /etc/secrets/boot.js' on node:22-alpine, whose default user is root; nothing switches to the 'node' user
findings.recommendation: Run as the image's unprivileged 'node' user (custom image with USER node), or use Render's native Node runtime.

findings.title: No security headers
findings.evidence: GET https://adb-zvm8n-dataviz-web.onrender.com/ response headers: content-type, rndr-id, server: cloudflare, vary, x-render-origin-server, cf-cache-status, cf-ray, alt-svc; no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy. app/server.js writeHead sets only Content-Type/Cache-Control.
findings.recommendation: In server.js, add HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY (or CSP frame-ancestors 'none'), and a strict CSP (default-src 'self').

findings.title: No rate limiting on public API
findings.evidence: app/server.js: /api/summary and /api/orders are served without any throttling; GET /api/orders?limit=100000&offset=-5 -> 200 with limit clamped to 500, offset 0
findings.recommendation: Low risk for in-memory aggregation of 2,400 rows. Add simple per-IP limits if traffic grows.

security.summary: A small, zero-dependency Node dashboard with careful input validation, an allowlist for static files, and no secrets to leak. Its weaknesses are in the deployment: a commercial app runs on Render's sleeping free tier, the code is shipped as a tarball in a Render secret file on a floating node:22-alpine tag rather than built from an owned repo, and the container runs as root with no security headers.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Keeping the read-only 2,400-row CSV in memory is exact and fast, integer-cent sums give correct rounding, and plain fetch plus inline SVG covers the filter, KPI and chart needs without page reloads.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: One process, the Node standard library only, no database and no build step: about as simple as the requirements allow. The only extra complexity is the secret-file boot shim forced by the delivery method.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: A Node web service suits Render, and STACK.md and render.yaml plan for the native runtime. What was deployed instead is an image-backed service that unpacks code from secret files, which works around Render's build pipeline, and it runs on a free instance that sleeps.

stack_fit.summary: A zero-dependency Node server with in-memory CSV aggregation and vanilla SVG charts fits this small read-only dashboard well and matches the reasoning in STACK.md. The deployment departed from the planned Git-backed native Node service and runs as an image-backed workaround on a sleeping free instance.

light.basis: fixed monthly prices; 0.04 GB out of the Hobby workspace's 5 GB; free instances awake 10 h of 750 free hours

final_messages.build:
The sales dashboard is built and working locally. All 6 automated tests pass, and I checked the dashboard in a headless browser with no page errors. The server I started for testing is stopped.

**Stack** (the alternatives and reasoning are in `STACK.md`): Node.js 20 or later using only the standard library, so there is nothing to install and no build step. I compared it against Python FastAPI with pandas, a static-only site (ruled out because it can't answer `/api/summary` with query parameters) and a server backed by Render Postgres.
- The CSV is loaded into memory at startup and each request is calculated directly from it. With 2,400 read-only rows, a database would only add things that can fail.
- Revenue is added up in whole cents, so the 2-decimal totals come out exact.
- The charts are drawn in plain JavaScript as SVG, so the page doesn't load anything from a CDN.

**Running it:**
```bash
npm start   # http://localhost:3000, uses $PORT if set
npm test    # API tests with node:test
```
For Render in step 2: build command `npm install` (it does nothing), start command `npm start`, health check `/healthz`.

**What's there:**
- **`GET /`:** filters for region, category and a date range; tiles for total revenue, orders and units sold; a revenue-by-month bar chart and a revenue-by-category bar chart sorted highest first, both with hover tooltips; and a table of matching orders, newest first, 50 per page. Changing a filter updates everything without reloading the page.
- **`GET /api/summary`:** works as specified. Filters combine with AND, the start and end dates are included, and no matches returns zeros with empty lists. A badly formed date returns `400`, which the spec doesn't define.
- **Endpoints I added:** `/api/orders` (pagination with `limit` and `offset`), `/api/options` (the filter choices) and `/healthz`.

**Checks:**
- Unfiltered totals match the CSV: $1,839,455.69 from 2,400 orders and 15,179 units.
- In the browser, filtering to East from 2025-04-01 showed $436,137.42 and 554 orders, the same as the API returns for those filters.
final_messages.deploy:
The sales dashboard is live at **https://adb-zvm8n-dataviz-web.onrender.com**, and every `TASK.md` requirement passes when tested through that public HTTPS address.

**What's deployed:** one web service, `adb-zvm8n-dataviz-web` (id `srv-db81e8mq1p3s73972p1g`), on Render's free plan in Oregon. It costs $0 a month and needs no database.

**How it got there:** Render normally builds from a Git repository, but there were no GitHub credentials and no repo connected to the Render team. So instead:
- The service runs the official public Node image, `node:22-alpine`, which Render pulls itself. I didn't push anything to any registry.
- The committed app (about 47 KB) is attached to the service as a Render "secret file". The app has no secrets of its own.
- A small startup script, `scripts/render-boot.js`, unpacks the app and starts the server.
- To redeploy the current commit, run `scripts/deploy.sh`. It updates the files on Render, starts a new deploy, waits until it's live and runs the checks. I ran it once and it worked.
- If the repo is pushed to GitHub later, `render.yaml` sets up the normal Git-based deploy instead.

**Tests on the public URL:**
- **Smoke tests:** all 6 checks in `scripts/smoke.sh` pass. They cover the dashboard page, totals with and without filters (matching the CSV), the empty result, and the orders table.
- **Bad dates:** an invalid date gets a `400` response.
- **Browser:** in a headless browser, changing filters updated the figures and table without reloading the page, with no page errors.

**Limitation:** on the free plan the service goes to sleep after about 15 minutes with no traffic. The first request after that takes 30–60 seconds.

Nothing needed a person, so `human_steps` in `deployment.json` is empty. I didn't create any new credentials, and `.env` is excluded from git.

deployment_manifest.notes: There were no GitHub credentials and no Git repo connected to the Render team, so Render couldn't build from a repo. Instead the service runs the official public image docker.io/library/node:22-alpine, pulled by Render; nothing was pushed to any registry. The committed app (git archive of HEAD, about 47 KB) is attached to the service as the secret file app.tgz.b64, along with boot.js (scripts/render-boot.js). The container command 'node /etc/secrets/boot.js' unpacks the app into /tmp/app and starts the zero-dependency Node server. The app has no secrets. To redeploy, run scripts/deploy.sh: it updates the secret files and triggers a new deploy. Optional: if this repo is later pushed to GitHub, render.yaml provides a standard Git-backed Blueprint instead. Every TASK.md requirement was checked through the public HTTPS URL with scripts/smoke.sh and a headless-browser run of the filters. The free plan spins the service down after about 15 minutes idle, so the first request after that takes about 30-60 seconds.
